newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Wolford posts record year results.
newsitem.headline: Wolford posts record year results.

text.p: Vienna's raunchiest stock, luxury hosiery maker Wolford, on Friday posted record earnings for the full year 1996/97, despite major streamlining of distribution channels in its core markets.
Net profit for the full year ending April 31 rose 15 percent to 190.6 million schillings ($14.8 million) on group sales of 1.65 billion schillings, compared with 1.48 billion in 1995/96.
Pre-tax profit climbed 15.8 percent to 280 million schillings while the company said it would raise its dividend to 10 schillings from 7.5 last year.
"We want to start the real success story in the business year 1997/98," chief executive Fritz Humer told a news briefing.
Humer said the company had sacrificed 60 million schillings in turnover to effect reforms so it could build up its core markets in Germany, Austria and France.
Overall sales growth should rise 10 to 15 percent, with profits exceeding that level, he added.
Wolford fell short of its target of 200 boutiques by the end of the year, with only around 160 at present but forecast it would have a total of 280 by the end of the year 1997/98.

The luxury hosiery and lingerie maker, which supplies fashion houses such as Yves St Laurent and Versace has an export quota of 91 percent and has seen growth soar by 144 percent in the United States and over 40 percent in Britain.
"We expect the United States to become our second biggest market after Germany. The potential is enormous," Financial Director Karl Millauer said.
The company expects to open another 30 stores in the United States, where it hopes to make its debut on the New York stock exchange in March next year.
Millauer said that according to U.S. accounting standards GAAP net profit rose 10 percent to 186 million schillings while pre-tax profit climbed to 275.6 million from 238.1 million.
Analysts said the results were in line with expectations, but that growth could surge in the medium term, once a planned drive to improve Wolford's brand recognition had set in.

"I think this is a very strong brand story. I expect to see a period of consolidation for two years where growth is around 15 to 17 percent and then it could take off to around 20 percent," said Susanne Seibel, analyst at Merrill Lynch.
Earnings per share climbed to 38 schillings from 33.3. Seibel forecast EPS of 46.4 schillings next year and 55 the year after.
"Germany is the most imminent market right now, but there is also lots of potential in Benelux countries which have not yet been tapped," she noted.
The company has seen growth in Germany flag in recent years but it said a recent management change should prompt a pick-up in sales there.

Wolford is also targetting Japan, where it opened a flagship store in the capital, but said the crucial step would be to gain a foothold the big department stores. If this could be achieved, it predicted up to three digit growth there.
The company said it planned to kick off on the Vienna futures and options exchange in the near future, which it hoped would improve liquidity.
Wolford, which has just one production plant based in Bregenz near the border with Switzerland, said a bottleneck in production that had delayed deliveries had been cleared.
Wolford stock stood 29 schillings lower at 1,159 at 1250 GMT. ($ = 12.90 Austrian Schillings)
